piv_deform_pass — PIV estimate op

• Data kinds: image2d × image2d × flow2d → flow2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.piv_deform_pass(a, b, flow, info, window=32, overlap=0.5, peak='gauss3', window_func='hann', order=3) (to call the implementation directly, import pivops; pivops.piv_deform_pass(a, b, flow, info, window=32, overlap=0.5, peak='gauss3', window_func='hann', order=3); from the registry, opspiv.get("piv_deform_pass"))

• Return value through the ledger: fullseye.ledger.piv_deform_pass(...) returns only the declared out type flow2d (the underlying function also returns auxiliary values). When you need what was dropped, use fullseye.ledger.piv_deform_pass.raw(...) or call pivops.piv_deform_pass directly.

• Underlying return: (flow, info) -> flow2d

Usage

1 pass with window deformation. Correlates only after first warping the images themselves with the predicted displacement.

Integer shifting (shift of piv_cross_correlate) assumes that the displacement is constant within the window. In fields such as rotation or shear, where the displacement varies within the window, the correlation peak collapses, so the 2 images are warped in opposite directions by half the prediction each before correlating (central-difference deformation).

Args:

a, b: image pair.

flow: predicted displacement (2, h, w) (output of piv_multipass etc.).

info: its info (the window-centre coordinates are needed).

window / overlap / peak / window_func: settings of the new pass.

order: order of the interpolation used for deformation (3 = 3rd-order spline).

Returns:

(flow (2, h', w'), info). The returned displacement is the total displacement in original image coordinates.
